s1.syndrome_frame: Severe lower limb deformity and pain with abnormal bone density and laboratory findings
salient_findings: Osteopenia of the left femoral head
key_facts: Patient is a 32-year-old Caucasian woman
Patient has severe left knee pain
Patient has bilateral genu valgum deformity
Patient had trochanteric bursitis at age 22
Patient takes OTC vitamin D3 without calcium
Patient's height is 155 cm and weight is 58.5 kg
Patient's BMI is 23.8
Patient has no personal or family history of fractures or metabolic bone disease
Patient's Q-angle is 23°
Patient has osteopenia of the left femoral head
Patient has normal lumbar spine density
Patient's serum phosphate is low
Patient's total 25-hydroxyvitamin D and 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D are elevated
Patient's parathyroid hormone is low
Patient's FGF23 is undetectable
Patient has inappropriately normal phosphate excretion
Patient has normal urine calcium
Patient has bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis without stones

shortlist.label: Hypophosphatemic rickets with nephrocalcinosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has severe lower limb deformity, low serum phosphate, and bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis

shortlist.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, osteopenia, and a history of possible rickets, which are consistent with X-linked hypophosphatemia

shortlist.label: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, osteopenia, and a family history that is not clearly indicative of X-linked inheritance, making autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets a possibility

shortlist.label: Hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia and normal urine calcium, but the presence of nephrocalcinosis suggests a possible defect in renal phosphate reabsorption

shortlist.label: Dent disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has hypophosphatemia, nephrocalcinosis, and normal urine calcium, which are consistent with Dent disease, a rare X-linked recessive disorder

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of severe knee pain, bilateral genu valgum deformity, low serum phosphate, elevated vitamin D levels, and bilateral medullary nephrocalcinosis without stones is most consistent with hypophosphatemic rickets with nephrocalcinosis, which is characterized by impaired renal phosphate reabsorption and nephrocalcinosis.

rejected.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
rejected.why: The patient is a female, making X-linked hypophosphatemia less likely as it is typically seen in males.

rejected.label: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
rejected.why: There is no family history of the disease, which is often seen in autosomal dominant conditions.

rejected.label: Hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria
rejected.why: The patient has normal urine calcium, which does not support the diagnosis of hereditary hypophosphatemic rickets with hypercalciuria.

rejected.label: Dent disease
rejected.why: Dent disease typically presents with hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and kidney stones, which is not consistent with the patient's normal urine calcium and absence of kidney stones.
